The bitter mingled cup of ancient woes, hard to be borne, that befell here in the house of Atreus, was grievous to my inmost heart — but never yet did I endure such pain as this. All else I bore with set soul patiently. But now — alack, alack! — Orestes dear, the day-and-night-long travail of my soul, whom from his mother's womb a new-born child I clasped and cherished! Many a time my service was toilsome and unprofitable, when his shrill outcry called me from my couch! For the young child, before sense is born in it, has only a dumb thing's life and must be nursed as its own nature bids. The swaddled thing has no speech, whatever discomfort comes — hunger or thirst or some lesser weakling need — for the babe's stomach finds its own relief. All this knowing in advance, yet often surprised, it was mine to clean the swaddling clothes — poor I was nurse to tend and fuller to make white; two works in one, two handicrafts I took up, when the father laid the boy in my arms. before: Alas, alas, O sisters — we have toiled, much and vainly have we toiled and borne! Vainly! And all we have wrought, the gods have foiled, and turned us to scorn! He has slipped from the net, the one we chased; he has escaped us who should have been our prey. Overmastered by slumber we sank, and our quarry has stolen away. You, child of the high God Zeus — Apollo — have robbed and wronged us! You, a youth, have trampled down the right that belonged to a more ancient godhead. You have cherished your suppliant, that man — the slayer, the God-forsaken, the bane of a parent — by craft you have taken him out of our grasp. A god, you have stolen from us, the avengers, a matricide son! And who shall consider your deed and say it was rightly done? The sound of chiding scorn came from the land of dream; deep to my inmost heart I felt it thrill and burn, thrust like a strong-grasped goad to urge onward the chariot's team. Thrilled, chilled with bitter inward pain, I stand as one beneath the doomsman's scourge. Shame on the younger gods who tread down right, sitting on thrones of might! Woe on the altar of earth's central fane! Clotted on step and shrine, behold the guilt of blood, the ghastly stain! Woe upon you, Apollo! Uncontrolled, unbidden, you, prophet-god, have imbrued the pure prophetic shrine with wrongful blood! For you held too heinous a regard for man, too little heed of divine powers; and us, the Fates, the ancients of the earth, you deemed of no worth. Scornful to me you are — yet shall you not fend off my wrath from him; though to hell he flee, there too are we! He has slipped from the net, the one we chased; he has escaped us who should have been our prey. Overmastered by slumber we sank, and our quarry has stolen away. You, child of the high God Zeus — Apollo — have robbed and wronged us! You, a youth, have trampled down the right that belonged to a more ancient godhead. You have cherished your suppliant, that man — the slayer, the God-forsaken, the bane of a parent — by craft you have taken him out of our grasp. A god, you have stolen from us, the avengers, a matricide son! And who shall consider your deed and say it was rightly done? The sound of chiding scorn came from the land of dream; deep to my inmost heart I felt it thrill and burn, thrust like a strong-grasped goad to urge onward the chariot's team. Thrilled, chilled with bitter inward pain, I stand as one beneath the doomsman's scourge. Shame on the younger gods who tread down right, sitting on thrones of might! Woe on the altar of earth's central fane! Clotted on step and shrine, behold the guilt of blood, the ghastly stain! Woe upon you, Apollo! Uncontrolled, unbidden, you, prophet-god, have imbrued the pure prophetic shrine with wrongful blood! For you held too heinous a regard for man, too little heed of divine powers; and us, the Fates, the ancients of the earth, you deemed of no worth. Scornful to me you are — yet shall you not fend off my wrath from him; though to hell he flee, there too are we! And he, the blood-defiled, shall feel and rue, even were I not there, the fiend-wrath that shall never end, descending on his head who foully slew.
